name: Block Action
desc: Triggers a block action animation/event (chest open, piston extend, note block play, etc.).
notes: Block actions: chest open/close, piston extend/retract, note block note, door open, dispenser click, etc.

writeup.p: S24 is a block-level event trigger: chest open/close, piston extend/retract, note block note, dispenser click, door open, beacon power. It carries a BlockPos, two action bytes (event ID and parameter) and the block type. The server broadcasts it from WorldServer's block-event queue (line 934 in the 1.8.9 corpus) to every player within 64 blocks of the position via sendToAllNear, which means it is a proximity event, not a per-player one.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleBlockAction calls PacketThreadUtil.func_180031_a then world.addBlockEvent(pos, blockType, data1, data2), which fans out to every IWorldAccess (render global, sound handler). The action bytes are interpreted per block: BlockChest uses data1 for open state, BlockNote uses data1 as the pitch index, BlockPiston uses data1 as the direction and data2 as extend/retract. The block type field is a cross-check; the client only plays the event if the local block matches.

Zero module hits in the 8-client corpus. The only non-vanilla reference is Rise 6.x's script API (NetworkAPI.java), which registers the packet class so Lua scripts can listen, not a shipped module. The reason is structural: S24 describes transient animations, and every piece of information it carries (chest open state, piston position) is already derivable from the block state or from S23 block changes, so ESP and chest modules read the world instead of the packet stream.

S24 is entirely cosmetic and server-trusted, so there is no meaningful exploit surface. The 64-block broadcast radius is the only measurable property, and it is too coarse for tracking. A malicious server could spam S24 with garbage data bytes, but the vanilla handler bounds the damage to a single addBlockEvent call per packet, and the local-block cross-check drops mismatches, so there is no crash or desync primitive.

implementation.overview: A cosmetic block-event trigger (chests, pistons, note blocks) broadcast within 64 blocks. No module in the 8 clients consumes it; the only non-vanilla reference is Rise 6.x's scripting API registration. Every fact it carries is derivable from block state, which is why clients ignore it.
implementation.server_handling: WorldServer keeps a BlockEventData queue; each tick it drains entries and sends S24 via mcServer.getConfigurationManager().sendToAllNear(x, y, z, 64.0D, dimensionId, packet). The 64.0 range is hardcoded in the server handler, matching the client's sound-render distance for block events. No rate limiting, no validation of the action bytes.
implementation.protocol_notes: Wire format: BlockPos long, byte action ID, byte action parameter, VarInt block registry ID. The block type is read as a full Block object server-side via Block.getBlockById. The two bytes are raw event semantics decided by the block class, so the same byte values mean different things for a chest vs a piston.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Not monitored. Block-action packets carry no player motion, timing or position claims, so anti-cheats ignore them entirely. The only conceivable use is a server-side sanity check that a piston event is accompanied by an actual piston block change, which no major anti-cheat implements for 1.8.9.
implementation.general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent exists on all clients but no module registers for S24 in the corpus.
implementation.client_variations: All 8 clients keep the vanilla handler. Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 additionally expose S24 in their script NetworkAPI, which is a class-registration table, not module code.

anticheat.overview: The block-action packet (chest open, piston, note block) has a single corpus hit: Artemis registers a GPacketPlayServerBlockAction wrapper in its packet library so the abstraction layer can route the clientbound packet. The wrapper is a read-stub: its read() body is empty, and no Artemis check consumes the packet. No anticheat flags S24 or derives state from it, because it carries transient animation data with no movement, timing or position claim.

checks.name: Packet wrapper registration (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Register the block-action packet in Artemis's packet abstraction so clientbound traffic of this type is recognized by the pipeline.
checks.how_it_works: GPacketPlayServerBlockAction extends GPacket and is linked to the PacketPlayServerBlockAction interface via @PacketLink. The read() method is empty, so the wrapper decodes no fields; it exists purely so the packet has a typed class in the cc.ghast.packet wrapper tree. No check in the corpus reads its payload.
checks.detects: Nothing. The entry documents the only anticheat touch point for S24: packet-library plumbing, not detection logic.
checks.variations: No other anticheat in the corpus references S24PacketBlockAction or PacketPlayOutBlockAction.
